subject: Private Offer drawdown plan — Horizon Health
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <procurement@horizonhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Menon <aisha.menon@horizonhealth.com>, Horizon Health Legal <legal@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Initial private-offer drawdown cadence (Horizon Health)

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We discussed pursuing a GCP private offer for Redwood to get committed spend in place for the next 12 months. Before we loop Legal, procurement needs a clear picture of the drawdown cadence so we can plan our ledger and the internal PO schedule.

Can you share:
- your recommended monthly SKU-level burn plan (we're starting at a 6-month pilot then scaling)
- any frontload or minimum drawdown expectations for marketplace redemption
- an outline of invoicing cadence and where marketplace credits will be visible in GCP billing

We'd like something by EOW if possible so we can align with our finance commit for Feb. Attaching a simple template for the PO numbers we expect to send once terms are locked.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Sr. Procurement Manager
Horizon Health

Attachment: Horizon_PO_Initial.xlsx (xlsx, 34KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <procurement@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial private-offer drawdown cadence (Horizon Health)

Hi Sanjay — appreciate the clear ask. Small summary here and attaching a term sheet and our recommended drawdown cadence so your finance team can map to the PO.

Quick answers up front:
- Typical drawdown profile: 20% frontload in month 1 (to cover onboarding + burst usage), then linearized monthly drawdown across the committed term (we can do 6- or 12-month phasing).
- SKU breakdown: we'll provision a mix of general-purpose and accelerated inference SKUs. The term sheet includes example SKU mappings and token-equivalent conversions for forecasting.
- Invoicing: GCP Marketplace will show the private-offer credits in the invoice line items as a redemption. Redwood invoices for committed overage/settlement only when redemption doesn't fully apply; we can set monthly reconciliation windows.
- Marketplace credits visibility: credits appear on the GCP billing export the month the offer is redeemed. We'll provide an example ledger mapping so your finance team can match the redemption against usage.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm desired commitment length (6 vs 12 months) and the target average monthly $ burn.
2) We exchange a redlineable term sheet (attached) + PO template filled by you.
3) Redwood opens the private-offer in GCP and provides the offer id + redemption cadence doc.

I've attached: RDW_GCP_PrivateOffer_TermSheet.pdf and a sample co-sell credit summary CSV. Ben — can you confirm if co-sell credits are handled via the marketplace listing or through separate crediting from GA?

Rachel Kim
Head of Marketplace Partnerships (Americas)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW_GCP_PrivateOffer_TermSheet.pdf (pdf, 120KB); co-sell-credit-summary.csv (csv, 4KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <procurement@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial private-offer drawdown cadence (Horizon Health)

Looping in finance and co-sell ops context. Short version:
- Co-sell crediting: for GCP private offers we can register the deal in the partner portal and route co-sell funds through the marketplace. Typically credits show up as a separate settlement line; for Horizon's case we recommend mapping the crediting to months 2-4 to avoid frontload mismatch.
- Burn smoothing option: if Horizon prefers even monthly realized spend rather than the frontload spike, we can frontload Redwood-managed on-boarding credits (one-time) and reduce month-1 redemption to ~10% and spread the remainder across months 2–6. That keeps your internal amortization smoother for finance.

Operational asks for procurement: please share the PO number format and the internal GL account you want Redwood to reference on invoices. We also need confirmation on who will approve the DocuSign (legal signatory).

Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <procurement@horizonhealth.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jan 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial private-offer drawdown cadence (Horizon Health)

Thanks all — confirming the operational timeline from Redwood: 
- Day 0 (after signed PO + term sheet): we open private offer and provide the Offer ID (T+2 business days).
- Week 1: offer visible in your marketplace console; we run a short verification test with your billing team to show credit redemption lines.
- Month 1: recommended minimal redemption = 15–20% of committed $ (or lower if Horizon requests smoothing).
- Monthly reconciliation: Redwood will provide an invoice reconciliation packet within 5 business days of month close.

Sanjay — if Horizon signs by Jan 30 we can align the first redemption for early Feb billing. Please confirm:
1) commitment length (you mentioned pilot — confirm 6 months)
2) target average monthly $ (fill in the attached Horizon_PO_Initial.xlsx and return)
3) legal signatory name/email for DocuSign

I'll kick this over to our billing ops once we have the PO.

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
